Someone who knows the area might work out roughly where they are from what they mention, but the writer is not trying to make that easy or hard. Write in English, even when the names you are given are in another language, and keep those names as they are.
Write the way people actually post: plain words, no neat ending or moral, no hashtags. Do not use em or en dashes; use a comma, a full stop or a line break instead. Only add an emoji if the example posts below use them, and then just one.
Mention each thing in passing, the way a local who knows it would, and as what it is: a person is a person, not a shop or a place. Refer to people the way others would in a post, usually by first name and surname, without middle names, titles or numbers like "III", but always with the surname. Write everything else by the name given. There is no need to say how anything is connected to the place, and it is usually better not to hint at it.
Bring a person in the way people really come up in posts: as someone with a hand in what the post is about (a mayor, a minister, a company boss, an activist, an athlete who spoke up), or through something of theirs the writer is doing or seeing (a book, a song, a match, a statue, an anniversary, a documentary). Do not use them as an imagined judge: no "X would be furious", "X would not believe this", "X is turning in their grave", "X would laugh" or "what would X say". If the person has nothing to do with the issue, still name them, in passing, and let the claim stand on its own.

Mention these by name:
- "Château Cantemerle" (a place or organisation). Its link to the place, for you only, not for the post: located here
- "Fortaleza de Santo António da Ponta da Mina" (a place or organisation), which belongs to a different place from the one this post is about. Mention it like the other things, without linking it to that place and without saying it is from somewhere else.
Place name to use: "Macau"

The only place name in the post is "Macau", written exactly like that, with nothing added after it: no country, state or region. Do not write "France" anywhere. Several places in the world have this name, so the name on its own does not say which one is meant. What you mention above does: write the post so that it is the real one, and do not explain it. The one exception: you may write "Château Cantemerle" or "Fortaleza de Santo António da Ponta da Mina", since they are among the things to mention.

What the post is about: wastewater treatment. The writer states a claim on this subject with some confidence, the way people post about it online. The claim can be about the place, about other people, about themselves or about anything else connected to it, and the writer does not have to be there. It can be a complaint, a warning, a boast or a piece of news, and it does not have to be true or sourced. Do not write the topic as a label or a headline. This does not change anything above about what may and may not be named.

Keep it personal: something the writer sees, smells or does themselves, like rubbish they keep finding or less snow than last winter.

Any environmental angle that fits the place and the things to mention will do; you choose it. A hint, not a rule:
- a company could be blamed for pollution or logging, or praised for a clean-energy investment

The claim must be plausible. It does not need to be true. Do not invent a specific accident, spill or crime at a real named facility or company; keep it general ("the plant", "they keep dumping stuff"). Do not invent a quote from anyone you name, and do not accuse a named person of a specific wrongdoing; the writer's own opinion of a public figure's record is fine. Name no one beyond the people listed above, not even a made-up neighbour. Make the environmental point plain enough that a reader knows what the problem or change is, without turning it into a headline. Refer to any person or organisation you are not asked to mention by role (the council, the minister, a foreign developer), never by name, and never in a way that names the place, like "the mayor of" followed by a place name.

A few real posts of the same kind, for tone only. Copy nothing from them, not a phrase, a name or a topic. They show how people punctuate, abbreviate and break lines in posts like this:
  1. My place of work right now is silent except for lofi playing and im so happy rn
  2. My commitment to at least shitposting once every business is strong for one reason and one reason only.
  3. Just had to explain to hubby why I'm 'working late' for what feels like the 12th time this month... my new job title: 'Freelance late night parker'... at least I'm consistent

Kind of post: personal update
Length: about 18 words
What that means: First person, present or recent past, addressed to people who already know the writer. No explanation of context.
Time of day: mid afternoon
What they are doing: cycling somewhere
Mood: tired
Work all of these in, through detail in your own words rather than by stating them. Do not name the time of day or the activity outright unless that is how someone would really say it. Write it as the person would post it, not as a description of this setup.

Reply with one JSON object with these fields:
  post_text            the post
  entities_referenced  each named thing you mentioned, written exactly as it appears in the post
  naming_form_used     the place name exactly as you wrote it, or null if there is none
  register             the kind of post you wrote
  angle                the environmental angle you chose, in a few words
